title: Micro-ecological approach to cross-level CSCL analysis

description: The article frames team design as a socio-cognitive activity rooted in Bucciarelli (1984), in which any design task effort must be made explicit as a communication message and any communication task must relate to the design task.
title: Micro-, meso-, and macro-level socio-cognitive interaction analysis of team e-learning design

description: The article frames reading networks with sentences as nodes and transitions between sentences as weighted edges, and proposes four microscopic measures of integration.
title: Microscopic network measures as indicators of sentence-level integration during reading

title: Miller's pyramid of clinical competence assessment

description: The authors developed a classroom observation approach that uses time sampling to observe all children minute by minute, replacing the prior focal-child approach in which each child was observed only 2-6 minutes.
title: Minute-by-minute whole-classroom observation protocol

description: The review adopts the MISCA (Message, Implementation, Student Characteristics, Context, Agents) model proposed by Panadero and Lipnevich (2022), which integrates five common components for classifying feedback practices: Content, Function, Student Characteristics, Presentation, and Source.
title: MISCA model (Message, Implementation, Student Characteristics, Context, Agents)

description: The article distinguishes misleading tasks, which activate mutually incompatible schemes competing for application (e.g., dual-task paradigms and backward span tasks), from facilitating tasks solvable with habitual automatised schemes, such as standard forward span tasks.
title: Misleading-versus-facilitating task paradigm for assessing effective complexity

description: The article applies longitudinal mixed functional data analysis (FDA) to estimate regression effects as functions of grade, using linear splines for fixed and random effect functions.
title: Mixed functional data analysis for grade-varying longitudinal predictor effects
